reference_materials: Seven native manufacturer AC28VS photographs inspected locally; not redistributed.
Manufacturer Australian catalogue page 13 rendered and inspected; nearby AC24VS photograph excluded.
findings: Sixteen final browser captures visually inspected: three openings from two directions, both scale faces, two internal views and six actual tripod outer-nut placements.

The continuous forged head/handle outline, real hanging hole, two web recesses, curved jaws, adjustment window and protruding slider stem follow the selected product photographs. Local outlines and finishes remain inferred.
Ordinary metric and inch graduations are independently typeset and calibrated to the fixed jaw datum. Both faces are readable; no additional robot markers were introduced.

The internal view hides the fixed body and scale planes to expose the real rack, continuous helical worm, axle and inferred axial spring. The selected spring layout is unobserved and remains unresolved.

At the six actual outer jam nuts, two of six examined clockings each are clear. Twenty-four intersecting poses remain in the report. Approximately 6.79 mm of the actual 6.8 mm nut is inside the jaw thickness; no insertion, rotation or torque success is claimed.
The rigid staged pose rests on actual worm/body contacts. The independently varied steel-density hypotheses keep the mass centre inside the support polygon by at least 2.35 mm.

Service geometry checked again after staging the grease tube: the same twelve clear nut poses remain. All sixteen re-rendered inspector captures are byte-identical to the previously inspected captures.

After adding the separate tape-measure candidate to the laboratory, service checks were rerun: 12 clear and 24 rejected static wrench poses are unchanged. All 16 wrench browser captures are byte-identical to the preceding inspected release; only the dependency records changed.
geometry_limits: Original source-constrained reconstruction, not manufacturer CAD or measured surface geometry. Exact local contours, tooth pitch, guide clearances, spring construction and manufacturing tolerances remain hypotheses.
Overall height and jaw-width source datums are unspecified; actual open envelopes are retained rather than forced to match an unknown source state.
No validated worm/rack transmission, spring preload, retention, settling, hand grasp, inner-nut access, paired counterholding, force or robot action.
